title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies mammalian enzymes catalyzing the second step of carnitine biosynthesis
summary: The OSMES workflow screened AlphaFold-modeled vitamin-B6-dependent enzymes by docking the substrate into active sites and ranking catalytically favorable conformations. It identified human SHMT1/2 as enzymes with hydroxytrimethyllysine-aldolase activity, validated in vitro; mouse Tha1 showed much higher catalytic efficiency, supporting a species difference in the pathway. The authors infer that humans may have lost a dedicated gene, with SHMT activity partly compensating.
ai_technology: OSMES (One Substrate–Many Enzymes Screening), automated structure-based docking/ranking workflow using AlphaFold models
organization: University of Parma; University of Padua; Sapienza University of Rome; CNR Institute of Molecular Biology and Pathology

evidence.tested: It identified human SHMT1/2 as enzymes with hydroxytrimethyllysine-aldolase activity, validated in vitro; mouse Tha1 showed much higher catalytic efficiency, supporting a species difference in the pathway.
evidence.unknown: Enzyme activity was validated in vitro. The claim about loss of a dedicated human gene is an evolutionary inference, not a direct gene-knockout demonstration; the authors note unresolved pathway questions.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked candidate enzymes for a specified metabolic reaction using docked substrate conformations and catalytically favorable active-site geometry; guided biochemical testing that verified SHMT1/2 activity.
